displayName: Deploy freshness — main merged but not deployed

conditions.displayName: Deployed commit drifted from GitHub main, or the repo moved

conditionMatchedLog.filter: resource.type="cloud_run_revision" AND resource.labels.service_name=("options-wheel-strategy" OR "covered-call-engine") AND (jsonPayload.event_type="deploy_freshness_drift" OR jsonPayload.event_type="deploy_freshness_repo_unreachable" OR textPayload:"deploy_freshness_drift" OR textPayload:"deploy_freshness_repo_unreachable")

documentation.content:
The scheduled /regression deploy-freshness check found that what is SERVING is not what is on GitHub `main`.

Two events trip this policy:

- `deploy_freshness_drift` — main is ahead of the deployed commit by more than DEPLOY_FRESHNESS_MAX_HOURS (default 2h). The merge happened; the deploy did not.
- `deploy_freshness_repo_unreachable` — either GitHub REDIRECTED the repo (it was renamed or moved: this is the FC-081 failure mode, and the `Location` header in the message names the new repo) or returned 404 (deleted, made private, or access lost). **A rename is a 301, not a 404** — the check disables redirect-following specifically so the rename is visible, because GitHub keeps a rename redirect alive indefinitely while the Cloud Build trigger, which matches the old literal name, silently stops firing.

Why this policy exists: the build-failure alert watches builds that START. A build that never starts fires no failure alert. FC-031 sat undeployed 11 days behind a red build; FC-081 sat undeployed 16 days because a repo rename detached the trigger and no build ever ran.

DETECTION LATENCY — this is not a real-time alert. The check runs on the /regression schedulers: `:45`, 10:45-15:45 ET, weekdays only. That is SIX runs per day, none of them overnight or on a weekend. A trigger that dies on a Friday evening is first reported at 10:45 ET Monday. Do not read silence outside those hours as health.

Triage:
  # what is serving
  curl -s https://options-wheel-strategy-799970961417.us-central1.run.app/health | jq .git_commit
  # what should be serving
  git ls-remote https://github.com/memon1987/agentic_options_wheel refs/heads/main
  # did a build even run?
  gcloud builds list --limit=5
  gcloud beta builds triggers list

If the message says the repo redirected, repoint BOTH the GITHUB_REPO env var and the Cloud Build trigger — the trigger is the half that is actually broken. If no build ran for the merge commit, the trigger is detached; repoint it rather than deploying by hand.

KNOWN FALSE POSITIVES — all three are expected, none is a bug:

1. LOCAL COMMIT PUSHED LATE. The clock is the commit's COMMITTER DATE, not the push time. A change committed locally and pushed more than 2h later is already "stale" the moment it lands, so it pages once even though the build ran promptly. Accepted deliberately: the alternative is looking up the Cloud Build record for the commit, which adds an IAM dependency on the runtime service account (cloudbuild.builds.viewer) purely to soften an alert. This repo's workflow pushes immediately, so the case is rare.
2. DELIBERATE TRAFFIC PIN. While traffic is pinned to an older revision (a rollback, a canary hold), the deployed commit is INTENTIONALLY behind main and this policy will fire every run. Disable the policy for the duration of the pin and re-enable it when traffic returns to latest.
3. MANUAL BUILD. `gcloud builds submit` supplies no $COMMIT_SHA, so the revision comes up with an empty GIT_COMMIT. That is reported as `deploy_freshness_no_commit` — a degraded warn on the OTHER policy (deploy_freshness_degraded), never drift on this one.

The check reports `warn`, never `fail`, on any transient GitHub error (401/403/429/5xx, timeout, malformed body), so this policy does not fire on a GitHub outage.
